scope: Eight selected primary/practitioner/official sources. Not a systematic review; no complete-book reading claim. Design proposals are inferences requiring product validation.

sources.title: How gamification motivates: An experimental study of the effects of specific game design elements on psychological need satisfaction
sources.access_scope: Primary paper text: abstract, manipulation checks, results, and discussion passages. Publisher landing page returned 403; paper text was available through ResearchGate.
sources.finding: Different element groups affected different reported psychological needs; decision-freedom effects were absent.
sources.limitation: Grouped elements do not isolate a badge effect; 88 manipulation-check exclusions left N=331. The simulation differs from this trivia game.
sources.design_application: Use understandable activity feedback and test Passport meaning; do not assume rewards alone create motivation.
sources.claim_status: Source supports directional design reasoning, not a proven FACT//DUEL outcome.

sources.title: Test-Enhanced Learning: Taking Memory Tests Improves Long-Term Retention
sources.access_scope: Publisher-hosted primary study abstract; not the full paper.
sources.finding: Free recall of prose improved delayed retention relative to restudy; immediate performance favored restudy.
sources.limitation: Materials and free-recall tests differ from timed four-choice trivia. No inference of verified mastery or measured product learning.
sources.design_application: Offer optional untimed recall and separate attempts, reveals, scores, and self-ratings.
sources.claim_status: Evidence for an opportunity to retrieve; product effectiveness remains untested.

sources.title: How Gamification Affects Software Developers: Cautionary Evidence from a Natural Experiment on GitHub
sources.publication: 2021 IEEE/ACM 43rd International Conference on Software Engineering
sources.access_scope: Author-deposited manuscript metadata and abstract, v3 dated 10 May 2021.
sources.finding: Streak removal was followed by fewer long streaks and changes in weekend and single-contribution behavior.
sources.limitation: Developer behavior, observational natural experiment, not a randomized study of games or harm.
sources.design_application: Avoid daily-loss streak obligations and assess valued activity rather than counter maximization.
sources.claim_status: Illustrates unintended behavioral effects; no claim that all streaks are harmful.

sources.title: The Gamer’s Brain — Chapter 16: UX Strategy (published excerpt)
sources.publication: The Gamer’s Brain: How Neuroscience and UX Can Impact Video Game Design, CRC Press; excerpt published by GamesBeat
sources.access_scope: Accessible excerpt from Chapter 16 only. The author's About page links the excerpt. No complete-book reading claim.
sources.finding: The excerpt recommends coordinated UX practice and questioning why players care about a feature.
sources.limitation: Practitioner guidance, not a causal experiment or a product-specific result.
sources.design_application: Connect existing duel/review activities around a coherent purpose before expanding modes.

sources.title: The Game Development Strategy Guide — Chapter 1: What Makes Us Play (sample)
sources.publication: The Game Development Strategy Guide: Crafting Modern Video Games That Thrive, Rosenfeld Media
sources.access_scope: Publisher-hosted sample chapter, especially definitions and intentional-friction sections. No complete-book reading claim.
sources.finding: The sample differentiates enjoyable purposeful obstacles from unnecessary interface friction.
sources.limitation: Practitioner framework, not evidence that a proposed Passport improves outcomes.
sources.design_application: Preserve clear challenge in questions; simplify navigation, inspection, and session endings.

sources.title: Three.js WebGLRenderer documentation
sources.access_scope: Current official documentation: renderer requirements, info, setPixelRatio, setAnimationLoop, powerPreference, and dispose.
sources.finding: Current renderer uses WebGL2, exposes resolution and renderer metrics, and documents disposal.
sources.limitation: APIs do not establish actual performance. Low-power is a hint, not a guarantee. Check installed version before implementation.
sources.design_application: Decorative scene with static fallback, measured budgets, controlled resolution, and lifecycle cleanup.
sources.claim_status: Verified API documentation; numerical art budgets are proposed local targets.

sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 2.2.1: Timing Adjustable
sources.access_scope: Informative explanation of WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.1, Level A, including exceptions and definition of real-time event.
sources.finding: Describes turning off, adjusting, or extending content-set time limits and narrow exceptions.
sources.limitation: This is explanatory guidance. An untimed Journal alone does not certify the game's conformance; bot play is not automatically a real-time exception.
sources.design_application: Untimed entry before play; no expiring navigation, explanations, rewards, or sources; separate timed-mode audit.
sources.claim_status: Accessibility design requirement reference, not a conformance assertion.

sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 2.3.3: Animation from Interactions
sources.access_scope: Informative explanation of WCAG 2.2 SC 2.3.3, Level AAA; motion preference and interaction-animation examples.
sources.finding: Nonessential interaction-triggered motion can be disabled; supports honoring reduced-motion preferences.
sources.limitation: This criterion is Level AAA and does not establish overall AAA conformance. Automatic animation is addressed separately by other criteria.
sources.design_application: Still default artifact, persistent motion control, no parallax/card flips under reduced motion, equivalent static states.
sources.claim_status: Accessibility design reference, not a conformance assertion.

retrieval_limitations: React Three Fiber Scaling Performance appeared in official search snippets but page fetches failed due to content size. It is not included as an independently reviewed source.
The Art of Game Design was located in search results but no reliable publisher excerpt was retrieved. No claim from that book is used.
The report evaluates product ideas from the supplied baseline, not source-code behavior or real player telemetry.
implementation_inferences: Finite persistent Passports connect duel, explanation, and recall activities.
Three deterministic cosmetic rewards express activity without competitive advantage.
Collection activity badges remain independent and do not imply mastery.
Results provide explicit session endings without automatic rematches.
Local event deduplication and catalog versions support truthful activity receipts.
Curiosity Press budgets are conservative project targets that require device measurements.
deferred_evidence_gates: Formative comprehension, source-finding, keyboard, and stopping-point playtests.
Separate timed-duel accessibility review and target-device performance measurements.
Delayed-recall comparison before claiming durable learning.
Observed item/player data and a fairness model before adaptive difficulty or ranked comparisons.
Question provenance and answer-quality review before catalog expansion.
